title: Double Trouble: Bilingual Pretraining Leaves Language-Conditioned Effects in Shared-Language Representations
abstract: arXiv:2608.26576v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When researchers compare multilingual models for probing, interpretability, or cross-lingual transfer, they often align embedding spaces and assume that shared-language representations are comparable. We show that this assumption can be premature for decoder-only models. We pretrain paired 310M-parameter models (one English-only, one bilingual) across eight typologically diverse languages, separately controlling for English exposure, total compute, and document overlap. After aligning on shared English vocabulary, we test held-out words and find that token embeddings look similar after alignment, but the deeper hidden states that the model uses for prediction do not. This gap holds for all eight languages and survives controls for document overlap and alternative alignment methods. This hidden-state mismatch grows through middle transformer layers, suggesting that it arises from contextual processing rather than the input representations

translated_title: 双重麻烦：双语预训练在共享语言表示中留下语言条件效应
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26576v1 公告类型：新 摘要：当研究人员比较多语言模型以进行探针分析、可解释性或跨语言迁移时，他们通常对齐嵌入空间，并假设共享语言表示是可比较的。我们表明，对于仅解码器模型，这一假设可能为时过早。我们在八种类型多样的语言上预训练了配对的3.1亿参数模型（一个仅英语，一个双语），分别控制了英语暴露量、总计算量和文档重叠度。在对齐共享英语词汇后，我们测试了保留词汇，发现词嵌入在对齐后看起来相似，但模型用于预测的更深层隐藏状态却不相似。这一差距在全部八种语言中都存在，并且在对文档重叠度和替代对齐方法进行控制后依然成立。这种隐藏状态不匹配在中间Transformer层中增长，表明它源于上下文处理，而非输入表示。
tldr: 双语预训练在深层隐藏状态中引入语言条件效应，即使在对齐嵌入空间后，共享词汇的表示在预测层面仍不一致，源于上下文处理而非输入表示。
en_tdlr: Bilingual pretraining introduces language-conditioned effects in deep hidden states, where aligned embeddings appear similar but prediction-relevant representations remain inconsistent across languages, arising from contextual processing rather than input representations.
